title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Coverage
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare. They say your coverage will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They may use official-sounding language to scare you.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your coverage will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and pay a small fee today."
red_flags: Caller asks for your Medicare or Social Security number
Asks for payment over the phone
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you are worried.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups on Your Computer
how_it_works: A pop-up appears on your computer saying you have a virus. It tells you to call a number for help. If you call, the scammer may ask to access your computer or demand money to 'fix' the problem.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft Support now at 1-888-XXX-XXXX."
red_flags: Pop-up says you have a virus and gives a phone number
Person asks to control your computer
Asked to pay with gift cards or wire transfer
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number or give anyone access to your computer.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: Someone calls pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer. They say your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away. They may beg you not to tell anyone.
example_message: "Grandma, I’m in jail and need bail money. Please send $2,000 right away and don’t tell Mom or Dad."
red_flags: Caller says it's an emergency and asks for secrecy
Wants money sent fast (gift cards, wire transfer)
Voice may sound odd or connection is bad
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check if the story is true.

title: Social Security Suspension Scam
how_it_works: You get a call or email saying your Social Security number is suspended due to suspicious activity. The scammer says you must confirm your number or pay to fix the problem.
example_message: "This is the Social Security office. Your number has been suspended. Press 1 to speak to an agent."
red_flags: Threatens to suspend your Social Security number
Asks for your Social Security number or payment
what_to_do: Do not respond. The real Social Security office will never call and threaten you or ask for payment.

title: Package Delivery Text Message Scam
how_it_works: You get a text saying there is a problem with a package delivery. The message asks you to click a link to fix the issue or pay a fee. The link may steal your information or install malware.
example_message: "Your package is waiting for delivery. Please click here to update your address: [fake link]"
red_flags: Link asks for personal or payment information
what_to_do: Do not click the link. Delete the message and contact the delivery company using their official website if you are expecting a package.
